advancements.steveparty.guide.lay_the_bo: Place a Tile, an Advanced Tile or a Checkpoint
advancements.steveparty.guide.make_a_paw: Get a Tokenizer Wand or a Token
advancements.steveparty.guide.mini_games: Get a Mini-Game Page or place a Mini-game Controller
Get a Shopkeeper Key or place a Trading Stall
advancements.steveparty.guide.root.descr: Get Plastic Pellets or a first board item
advancements.steveparty.guide.root.title: Steve Party Maker
The redstone power a space receives (0-15) picks its active slot: power 0 = slot 1, power 1 = slot 2…

Role, colour and destinations follow the active cartridge: one space can be blue, then red, then a Stop. A comparator or a redstone counter makes spaces that change every turn.
book.steveparty.guide.board.board_view.p: With the Wrench in hand (48 blocks), each link shows as moving chevrons. Each space wears a plate: steps from the start, **Start**, a gold **?** at forks, a red **!** at dead ends, an orange **!** when unreachable. Only you can see it.

Click the **Party Controller** with the Wrench, or run `/steveparty board check`, for a full diagnosis: no start, dead ends, shops without a trader, lonely teleports…

Operators can also use `/steveparty board copy`, `paste` and `template loop|line`.
book.steveparty.guide.board.linking.desc: Trace the path with the Wrench
book.steveparty.guide.board.linking.name: Linking Spaces
book.steveparty.guide.board.linking.page:
The Wrench has 3 modes (**R** or sneak + scroll):
- **Trace**: click spaces one after another to link them; click the first one again to close the loop.
- **Edit**: pick an origin, then add or remove links from it.
- **Cut**: removes every outgoing link.

Hold right-click and sweep to link a whole path (up to 32 blocks).

Missing cartridges are taken from your inventory (free in creative); a cartridge in your off hand sets the type of new spaces.

Left-click in the air to **undo** (sneak: redo), 32 steps. Tiles turn to face their destination. With the Wrench in your off hand, each Tile you place is linked to the previous one.
book.steveparty.guide.board.moving.name: Moving on the Board
book.steveparty.guide.board.moving.page0:
Each Tile reached = 1 step; a Checkpoint = 0. At a fork, arrows appear for the pawn's owner: right-click one with an **empty hand** to choose.

When the steps run out, the space's role fires: a jingle, particles in its colour and a message for everyone in the party.
book.steveparty.guide.board.name: The Board
book.steveparty.guide.board.placing.name: Placing Tiles
book.steveparty.guide.board.placing.page:
A Tile faces one of **8 directions** (45° steps), following your gaze.

- On stairs it follows the slope: tiles on a staircase form a ramp.
- On stair corners it tilts diagonally.
- On bottom slabs, snow or carpet it sits on their surface.

Pawns stand on the surface and walk slopes like stairs.
book.steveparty.guide.board.router.name: Redstone Router
book.steveparty.guide.board.router.page0:
Put a cartridge in the **Board Space Redstone router**: its destinations are the spaces to drive. The power the router receives **replaces** theirs, so one lever can switch a whole board.

A comparator on the router catches events: a 10-tick pulse when a pawn stops on a linked space, at the level of its role, and level 1 when one passes.
book.steveparty.guide.board.router.page1:
- 15: plain space
- 14: bonus
- 13: malus
- 12: empty item space
- 11: start
- 10: Stop
- 9: Roll Again
- 8: Teleport
- 7: forward
- 6: back
- 5: shop stop
- 4: star space
- 1: a pawn passes
book.steveparty.guide.board.sizes.name: Tile Sizes
- **Standard**: a 2x2 picture centred on its block.
- **Small**: exactly one block.
- **Large**: exactly 2x2 blocks.

Stonecutter: 1 tile gives 2 small. Crafting: 2 small make 1 standard, 4 standard in a square make 1 large, and a large one splits back into 4.
Break a Tile with **Silk Touch**: it drops as a single item that keeps all its cartridges, their settings, its look and its size. Without Silk Touch, the cartridges drop on the ground.

A Tile holding cartridges cannot change size at the crafting table.
book.steveparty.guide.board.spaces.name: Tiles & Checkpoints
book.steveparty.guide.board.spaces.page0:
A board is made of spaces. Each space holds **cartridges** that give it a role and its next destinations.

- **Tile** (grey rim): 1 cartridge, counts as a step.
- **Advanced Tile** (gold rim): 16 cartridges, redstone picks the active one.
- **Checkpoint**: 16 cartridges, does **not** count as a step.
book.steveparty.guide.board.spaces.page1: Any carpet colour works for the Tile.
book.steveparty.guide.board.spaces.page2: A floating glass cube without collision: pawns cross it for free, handy for turns and forks.
book.steveparty.guide.board.stamping.des: Give a tile its own look
book.steveparty.guide.board.stamping.pag:
Hold a **Stencil** and a **dye** (one in each hand), or use the **Stencil Hammer**, and right-click a Tile: it takes the dye colour with the pattern drawn darker. Costs 1 dye.

With a cartridge inside, the active cartridge is stamped and keeps its look once removed. A **wet sponge** wipes the stamp.
book.steveparty.guide.board.wrench.name: Wrench
book.steveparty.guide.board.wrench.page0: The **Wrench** links spaces, shows the board, opens cartridge blocks (**sneak** + right-click on a space or a router) and breaks any plastic block in one hit.
book.steveparty.guide.cartridges.advance:
A pawn ending its move here goes **1 to 6** spaces further: forward (green) or back (magenta). Sneak + scroll, cartridge in your main hand, sets the count and the direction.

Going back, it retraces its path. No chaining: landing on another such space does nothing more. Only during a party.
book.steveparty.guide.cartridges.cartrid:
Every cartridge has its own menu: right-click in the air while holding it, or open its space. A dye on the space recolours the active cartridge.

Each role below is a plain Cartridge plus one ingredient, shapeless.
book.steveparty.guide.cartridges.invento:
Gives or takes items. Right-click up to **8 chests** with it to link them; right-click in the air for its menu: 9 ghost slots, the **scroll wheel** sets the amount, and going below 1 makes it **negative**.

Selection: random, all, or cycle.

When a pawn ends its move on it, its owner receives the positive items, taken from the chests, and loses the negative ones, stored in the chests.

**Blue** = bonus, **red** = malus, **orange** = nothing to give. Blue and red also make the mini-game teams. The Party Controller bank, Looting Box and Piggy Bank use this cartridge too.
book.steveparty.guide.cartridges.name: Cartridges
When a pawn ends its move here on its player's turn, that player **rolls again** at once, and the spent die comes back.

The extra turn never gives another one.
book.steveparty.guide.cartridges.shop.pa:
On a **Tile**, the shop opens when a pawn **ends** its move there; in a **Checkpoint**, every passing pawn stops.

The player gets the trade screen of the nearest **Boxed Trader** that has stalls (32 blocks). Sneak + scroll sets how many items can be bought (1-9). Without a choice, the shop closes after 60 s.
book.steveparty.guide.cartridges.star.pa:
Makes a **yellow star space** (tile or Checkpoint). When a party starts, the **star** lands on one active star space at random: a big Power Star floats over it.

A pawn passing over it stops; with enough coins, its player chooses in the chat to **buy** it (20 coins by default; bought by itself after 15 s). The star then moves to **another** star space.

In its menu: the **price**, sold **in passing** or only **on stopping** (a Checkpoint always sells in passing), and whether the star **leaves** a space switched off by redstone.

No active star space: the star hides until one is switched on. The Skeleton Key never skips it.

Fill the **Party Controller's chests** (its bank, on the Gains page) with **stars**: each star sold is taken from them, and the coins paid go back into them (what does not fit falls by the controller).

No star left in the bank: nothing is sold, the pawn goes on.
book.steveparty.guide.cartridges.start.p:
A pawn set on a start space **binds** to it: it floats, faces the nearest player, and the space takes the pawn's colour. Right-click with an empty hand to own the space and its pawn.

The Party Controller only takes pawns bound to a start space. Hit the pawn to unbind it.
book.steveparty.guide.cartridges.stop.pa:
Turns a space into a charcoal **Stop** space with a no-entry sign. A pawn that reaches it **ends its move** there, whatever steps remain.

It works on a Checkpoint too.
book.steveparty.guide.cartridges.telepor:
A pawn ending its move here jumps to **another Teleport space of the same colour** on the board, at random or in turn. Networks: purple (default), green, orange or blue; a dye on the space changes it.

In its menu: stay on arrival or step one space further, and whether that space fires.
book.steveparty.guide.decoration.buildin:
Two families, 8 shapes per colour: **Polished Terracotta** (17 colours) and **Polished Concrete** (16): block, bevelled bricks, stairs, slab, wall, and the brick versions.

2×2 terracotta or concrete gives 4 polished blocks; 2×2 polished gives 4 bricks. The stonecutter skips steps.
Two polished blocks of different colours in a 2×2 checkerboard give 4 **Polished Tiles** (concrete or terracotta). Swap the colours for the shifted pattern; the stonecutter makes single-colour tiles.
book.steveparty.guide.decoration.floatin:
Plastic blocks rise through still water and ride **bubble columns** (up on soul sand, down on magma), carrying whatever stands on them, without ever crushing anyone.

A block over soul sand makes a fast water elevator. A **chain** holds a piece in place. Slabs, stairs and walls never float.
A wooden drum hammer loaded with **9 stencils and 9 dyes** (sneak + right-click). Sneak + scroll changes the stencil or the colour (**G** switches which). Right-click to **stamp**: a drum thud, a paint splash and the pattern printed, 1 dye per hit.

The last colour, *Engrave*, uses no paint.
book.steveparty.guide.decoration.hop_swi:
Makes target blocks **disappear or appear** for a while. Right-click each target with a Cartridge, then put it in the switch. Jump on it or power it: it stays down for the duration, then pops back up and **launches** whoever stands on it.

Modes: toggle, appear, disappear. A **clock** changes the duration (sneak: shorter). All plastic is switchable.
book.steveparty.guide.decoration.name: Decoration
book.steveparty.guide.decoration.paintin:
- Dye alone: repaints the symbol.
- Glow ink sac: the paint glows at night.
- Sponge: stops the glow.
- Wet sponge: erases everything.
- Brush (held): fades the symbol, gone after 5 strokes.

Paint on walls, floors and ceilings is a thin layer that hitting can't break.
book.steveparty.guide.decoration.pipes.p:
Mario-style pipes. Placed against a pipe or its mouth, they connect. Enter a mouth (right-click, sneak in front of it, or fall in): you shoot through and come out of another end at random.

A pipe going into a solid block teleports to the nearest mouth of that colour within 100 blocks.
6 plastic blocks, or 4 + 2 glass for a windowed pipe. Glass pipes: 6 glass.
book.steveparty.guide.decoration.plastic:
4 Plastic Pellets + 1 dye + 1 amethyst shard give 4 blocks. Neighbouring blocks of the same colour merge into a single piece (up to 4×2×4).

The Wrench breaks plastic in one hit; shears are fast too.

- **Plastic Stud**: 1 block gives 4; sticks to floor, wall or ceiling, needs no support.
- **Slabs, stairs, walls**: usual recipes or the stonecutter.
- **Plastic Stick**: 2 blocks give 4.
- **Fence**: blocks and sticks; it carries road signs.
book.steveparty.guide.decoration.signs.p:
Panels and road signs: sneak-click the top of a fence or wall to stand on it, click its side to hang it, any other face to lay it flat.

Material recipes need the **same** block everywhere: no half-oak, half-birch sign.
A plastic block over pellets gives 2. Off a post, it floats like plastic.
book.steveparty.guide.decoration.stencil:
Right-click it with a stencil, then again to open the editor: left-click cuts a pixel, right-click fills it, drag to draw lines. Flip, rotate, invert, undo.

Your **library** (128 patterns, kept on death) learns every patterned stencil you carry. Click a pattern to copy it for free.

A **Stencil** holds a 16x16 pattern. Stencil in one hand, dye in the other: right-click a sign or any full block face to paint it (1 dye). A stencil alone **engraves** a sign. The stencil is never used up.

Copy one with blank stencils. 50 patterns can be found in structure chests.
book.steveparty.guide.gadgets.looting_bo:
Open it with the Wrench and insert an **Inventory Cartridge** linked to a chest. Jump and **headbutt** it from below: it drops items from the chest (all, next or random, per the cartridge mode). Two hits, then 3 s of rest.

Tip: leave 2-3 blocks of air below it.
book.steveparty.guide.gadgets.name: Gadgets
book.steveparty.guide.gadgets.plunger.pa: Right-click a mob: silenced! Again: it gets its voice back.
book.steveparty.guide.gadgets.shoes.name: Triple Jump Shoes
book.steveparty.guide.gadgets.shoes.page: Chain jumps less than 1.5 s apart: the 2nd one is ×1.5 higher, the 3rd ×2, then the cycle starts over.
Leather boots, a rabbit's foot and 2 slime balls.
book.steveparty.guide.gadgets.villager_m:
A Villager Block reacts to about 70 things with 16 faces: it waves when you arrive, blushes when stared at, drools when you eat, panics at zombies, dances to a jukebox (wild on Pigstep), begs when you break it…

Give it bread or a flower, or click it 10 times quickly and watch it see stars.
book.steveparty.guide.getting_started.fi: Six steps to a working board

1. Craft **Tiles** and lay out a path.
2. Link them with the **Wrench**.
3. Put a **Start Cartridge** in the first Tile.
4. Turn a mob into a pawn with the **Tokenizer Wand** and set it on the start.
5. Place a **Party Controller** and press *Start party*.
6. Roll a die!

Each step has its own tab in this book: *The Board*, *Cartridges*, *Pawns & Dice* and *Running a Party*.

Shops, the Mula and decoration can come whenever you like.
book.steveparty.guide.getting_started.pl: The first ingredient of almost everything

Almost everything starts with **Plastic Pellets**: smelt **sugar cane** in a furnace.

Pellets go into Tiles, Cartridges, Tokens, plastic blocks and road signs. Start a sugar cane farm early!
book.steveparty.guide.getting_started.we: What Steve Party Maker is about

Steve Party Maker turns Minecraft into a **party board game**: build a board block by block, turn any mob into a pawn, roll the dice, play mini-games and collect stars, all in survival.

Almost every part of it can be driven with **redstone**.

Entries open as you progress, like a star map. A locked entry tells you which milestone opens it: placing a Tile, placing a Party Controller, finding a star fragment…

Every item is in the mod's creative tab. With REI installed, you can also browse all the recipes.
book.steveparty.guide.lock.dice_forge: Place a Dice Forge to unlock this entry.
book.steveparty.guide.lock.lay_the_board: Place a Tile to unlock this entry.
book.steveparty.guide.lock.make_a_pawn: Get a Tokenizer Wand or a Token to unlock this entry.
book.steveparty.guide.lock.mini_games: Get a Mini-Game Page or place a Mini-game Controller to unlock this entry.
book.steveparty.guide.lock.open_shop: Get a Shopkeeper Key or place a Trading Stall to unlock this entry.
book.steveparty.guide.lock.party_time: Place a Party Controller to unlock this entry.
book.steveparty.guide.lock.roll_the_dice: Get a die to unlock this entry.
book.steveparty.guide.lock.stardust: Get a star fragment to unlock this entry.
book.steveparty.guide.mini_games.entranc:
A **Mini-game Pipe** is the way into a mini-game outside a party. Click it with the page to program it, then connect coloured pipes: enter by a green mouth to come out as a player, by a white one as a spectator…

Range: **copper** 100 blocks, **iron** the whole dimension, **golden** every dimension.
book.steveparty.guide.mini_games.formats:
A page lists its formats: **Teams** (2 to 4 sides, sizes from-to), **Free for all** or **All together**. Names build themselves: Duel, 2 vs 2, 1 vs all…

In a party, teams come from the board: **Team A** = pawns on a positive (blue) space, **Team B** = on a negative (red) one; neutral ones fill in. Only pages with a fitting format can be drawn.
book.steveparty.guide.mini_games.mg_cont:
Place it in the arena and click it with the page. Its lamp shows the state: **red** idle, **orange** practice round, **green** real round.

Outside a party, **Play** starts the mini-game with the players within 5 blocks of its pipes; no rewards are paid. A redstone pulse plays, the next one stops.

In a party, a mini-game with a controller starts with a **practice round**: same teams, no rewards. It restarts until everyone is ready: press **Y** or the *Ready* button. Then the real round begins.

Turn practice off in the Party Controller settings.
book.steveparty.guide.mini_games.name: Mini-games
book.steveparty.guide.mini_games.pages.p:
A **Mini-Game Page** describes one mini-game. Right-click in the air to open its editor: title, description, image, then the **Formats**, **Pipes** and **Results** tabs.

Keep pages in a **Mini Games Catalogue** (91 slots) and put it in the Party Controller. A page + paper makes a linked copy.
book.steveparty.guide.mini_games.podiums:
Podiums record **who won**: the higher the column, the better the place. Sneak on one or right-click it to take it. Link podiums to the page (click with the page): the mini-game ends when every place is taken.

Placed like slabs, they stack into columns. During a linked mini-game, columns of the same height share one place.

A redstone pulse in a column does what the Wrench set: register the nearest player (default), give the best free place, clear it, or reset the group. Comparator: 15 while taken.

A Goal Pole Base touching a podium becomes the group's counter.
Gold, silver and bronze podiums are only looks.
book.steveparty.guide.mini_games.zone.pa:
In the page editor, *Draw zone* and right-click two corners (128 blocks per side at most). With the **Restore** option, each round is played apart in that zone: players leave their inventory at the door and play with an empty one, nothing crosses the border, and the arena is rebuilt afterwards.

*Adventure* stops players from breaking or placing blocks.
book.steveparty.guide.name: Steve Party Maker Guide
book.steveparty.guide.party.bell.name: Party Bell
book.steveparty.guide.party.bell.page0.t:
Right-click to choose when it pulses: party start, round start, turn start, die thrown, turn end, mini-game drawn, mini-game end, Event card, party end. Its comparator gives a matching number (die value, rank…).

Set to **wait** with the Wrench, it freezes the party until it receives a redstone signal.
book.steveparty.guide.party.cards.name: Party Cards
A plastic stud of the card's colour + paper + redstone gives 4 cards.
book.steveparty.guide.party.controller.p: **Restrict dice**: off, every die is allowed. On, only the dice in its slots may be thrown during the party (by default the Default Die and its power-up version). Click a slot with a die to add a copy, with an empty hand to remove it; the arrow shows the whole list.

It takes the pawns bound to a start space within 100 blocks. Press *Start party*, or send it a rising redstone edge.

A comparator reads the phase: 0 idle, 1 setup, 2 turn, 3 mini-game, 4 waiting for a bell, 5 end.

During a party, *Stop the party* (Status page, click twice) ends it at once, without a winner: a running mini-game is called off, every pawn goes back to its start space, out of the game, and a new party can start. Only an operator or a Game Master may; breaking the controller stops it too. Operators can also run `/steveparty party stop`.
book.steveparty.guide.party.flow.descrip: From the first roll to the podium
book.steveparty.guide.party.flow.name: How a Party Plays
book.steveparty.guide.party.flow.page0.t:
1. Bound pawns join.
2. Each owner rolls once: the highest goes first.
3. The program is built: by default, one turn per pawn then a mini-game, every round.
4. On its turn, a pawn's owner rolls and moves.
5. Mini-games pick teams and a page, then send the players through pipes.
6. The end: pawns are freed.
book.steveparty.guide.party.flow.page1.t:
If a pawn is missing (offline or unloaded), its turn waits 60 s and the chat offers **[Skip turn]** and **[Exclude]**. A restarting server resumes the current step.

Press **M** to arrange the party HUD, **H** to hide it.
book.steveparty.guide.party.goal_pole.de: Jump to the top and score
book.steveparty.guide.party.goal_pole.pa:
Place a **Goal Pole Base**, stack **Goal Pole** segments on it and hang **Flags**. Land on top of a segment: **1up**, a golden heart, no fall damage, and a point for the base.

The base counts landings (or any scoreboard criterion) for the party players, everyone, nearby players or a selector. Set it up with the Wrench.

Set a goal on a segment with the Wrench (at least 1 by default). Reached: the flag slides down and the gold ball lights up. A comparator on a segment gives 15 once reached; on the base, a pulse per point or the progress 0-15.

With *Goal: per player*, each player who reaches it takes the best free podium place.
Three wool in a corner shape; the wool sets the colour, 1-8 dyes retint it. Shears take it back.
book.steveparty.guide.party.name: Running a Party
book.steveparty.guide.party.piggy_bank.d: Give and take on a pulse
book.steveparty.guide.party.piggy_bank.p:
A ceramic pig with a coin slot. On each redstone pulse, it applies its Inventory Cartridge: it gives items from the linked chest and takes the negative ones. Right-click to pick the target: current player, last winners, all players, or the nearest.

In *all* mode it's all or nothing: sell a star for coins!
book.steveparty.guide.party.powerups.pag:
A **power-up** is used at the **start of your turn**, **before your roll**, and adds to it (a die with the Power-up module replaces the roll). Right-click it during your own turn: it is **consumed** only if it worked.

- **One** power-up per turn.
- Too late once your roll counts (a blank roll can still be rolled again).

- **Mushroom**: **+3** to your next roll this turn, with any die.
- **Double Coins**: the coins you **gain** this turn are **doubled**. Losses are not.
- **Padlock**: blocks **one** Thief Bell or Trap aimed at you, until your next turn. Kept if you are already protected.

- **Thief Bell**: pick a player (15 s, else the richest) and steal **5 to 15** of their coins.
- **Golden Thief Bell**: the same, for **one star**.
- **Trap**: hidden on your pawn's space. The next other player to stop there gives you **10** coins.

A Padlock parries them. A bell is kept if its target has nothing to steal.

- **Star Whistle**: the Star flies off to another Star space.
- **Golden Pipe**: your pawn warps just **before the Star**, then you roll your die.

The star is the Star Cartridge's. Both are kept when the board has none.

Power-ups are **easy to craft**: at most one Coin and one or two common items.

The **board's maker** chooses how players get them: a **Trading Stall**, the Boxed Trader, a Shop space, or an **Inventory space** handing out a chest's content.

Unpriced on a stall, in Coins: Mushroom **5**, Double Coins and Padlock **8**, Trap **10**, Thief Bell **12**, Whistle **15**, Pipe **25**, Golden Bell **40**.

During a party, a player carries at most **3** power-ups: **Max power-ups** on the Party Controller's Settings page (∞: no limit). **Dice with the Power-up module** count too, being spent; any other die is your own and does not.

At the limit, shops refuse to sell, Inventory spaces keep the extra in their chest, and power-ups on the ground stay there.
Mushroom: red mushroom + sugar + Coin. Double Coins: Coin + glowstone dust + paper.
Padlock: Coin + iron ingot + tripwire hook. Trap: Coin + stone pressure plate + string.
Thief Bell: Coin + gold ingot + string. Golden Thief Bell: Thief Bell + 2 gold ingots.
Star Whistle: Coin + bamboo + glowstone dust. Golden Pipe: Coin + 2 gold ingots + ender pearl.
book.steveparty.guide.party.rewards.name: Coins, Stars & Rewards
book.steveparty.guide.party.rewards.page:
A player's stars and coins are those items in their inventory; ranking goes by stars, then coins. Defaults: the **Coin** and the **Power Star** (change them in the Rewards tab).

Rewards are paid from chests: put an Inventory Cartridge linked to chests in the bank slot. The controller never creates coins or stars: only the star sold on a **star space** is made.
One gold nugget makes a Coin.
book.steveparty.guide.party.step_control:
Right-click to switch mode: **up** = next step, **side** = restart the step, **down** = previous step. A rising redstone edge applies it to the nearest Party Controller (64 blocks).

Linked to a Mini-Game Page, its pulse ends that mini-game with the podium places as they stand.
book.steveparty.guide.pawns_dice.dice.pa:
Right-click: the die flies to the **nearest mob** within 20 blocks (sneak: the nearest **player**), floats above its head and spins. **Hit** it to stop it.

The result moves one of the thrower's pawns within 25 blocks, 1.5 s later. During a party, only the pawn whose turn it is moves.

- **Default Die**: 1 to 10.
- **Double Dice**: two linked dice, 2 to 20.
- **Triple Dice**: three, 3 to 30.
- **Forged Die**: its own faces, from the Dice Forge.

A thrown die vanishes 2 s after its result and comes back to you (a Power-up die is spent).
Dice come out of the **Dice Forge**. Combine them for bigger ones; they split back.
book.steveparty.guide.pawns_dice.faces.p:
Faces are only used in the **Dice Forge**. 2 iron ingots + 2 nether quartz give 4 **Blank Dice Faces**; the **stonecutter** turns a blank face into any number (0 to 10, premium or cursed) and back.

On a forged die, a blank face is a 0.

- **Face 0**: stay put and replay the current space.
- **Coin +1 to +10**: the thrower gains coins.
- **Debt −1 to −10**: the thrower loses coins.
- **Swap**: swap places with another player's pawn.

With these faces, the pawn does not move.
Blank face + ender pearl, or + a Coin. Debt: blank face + spider eye.
book.steveparty.guide.pawns_dice.game_ma:
A treasure enchantment for the Tokenizer Wand only, found in woodland mansion chests (25%), or dropped by evokers (5%) and illusioners (25%) killed by a player.

With it, the wand resizes anyone's pawn and can `/steveparty exclude` any pawn of a party within 100 blocks. Operators already have these rights.
book.steveparty.guide.pawns_dice.name: Pawns & Dice
book.steveparty.guide.pawns_dice.pawns.p:
A pawn is a figurine: no AI, silent, invulnerable, it can't be pushed or leashed, and feeding or trading does nothing.

Its name is the mob's custom name, or yours. Its colour comes from the mob's texture and tints its octagonal base; right-click it with a dye to change it. Cast the spell on your own pawn again to resize it.
book.steveparty.guide.pawns_dice.token.p:
The **Token** is how you move a pawn by hand. Right-click your pawn with an empty Token to store it; right-click a block with the full Token to set it down, size, owner and colour kept.

Set it on a start space to enter it in the party.
Plastic Pellets and a shulker box.
book.steveparty.guide.pawns_dice.wand.de: Any mob can be a pawn
book.steveparty.guide.pawns_dice.wand.pa:
Right-click a mob with the **Tokenizer Wand** (or hold right-click in the air to shoot a spark up to 32 blocks): the *Pionificus!* spell opens.

Draw a circle around the mob: on the guide = a 1-block pawn, twice as big = 2 blocks (max), smaller = smaller, down to 0.25. Esc cancels. Not on the Ender Dragon or the Wither.
Wand: Garnet Crystal Ball, gold block, blaze rod. Ball: redstone blocks around a nether star.
book.steveparty.guide.shops.bandanas.pag:
Each trader wears one of 5 bandanas. **Shears** on an open trader steal it, and it hides for 20 s. Wearing a bandana, traders ignore you. Give one back to change a trader's colour.

Shear a bald trader again to steal its box look: a **Box Costume**. Wear it like a chestplate, and sneak to hide inside as a real-looking block.
book.steveparty.guide.shops.name: Shops
book.steveparty.guide.shops.overview.pag: A star fragment of any colour, a gold ingot and a gold nugget, in a column.
book.steveparty.guide.shops.owners.name: Owners & Protection
book.steveparty.guide.shops.owners.page0:
The first player to link a key to a trader **owns** it. Only the owner can link blocks, open the stall and register, open the stock chests or break the shop's blocks; explosions spare them.

One customer at a time. Hoppers can fill the stock chests and empty the registers.
book.steveparty.guide.shops.register.pag:
27 slots. After each sale, the payment goes into the linked registers, in order; if they're full, it drops near the trader, never destroyed. Each sale sends a 4-tick redstone pulse from every linked register.

Mine it with an iron pickaxe or better.
book.steveparty.guide.shops.stall.name: Trading Stall
Each column is an offer (9 at most): the item sold on top, **Price 1** and **Price 2** below. Prices must match exactly.

The top item is only a model: each sale takes the same item **from the linked chests**. Without stock, the offer is greyed out.
The two carpets give the awning its colours.
book.steveparty.guide.shops.trader.descr: A villager hidden in a box
book.steveparty.guide.shops.trader.name: Boxed Trader
book.steveparty.guide.shops.trader.page0:
A villager hidden in a box disguised as a block. It peeks out when a player comes within 15 blocks (sneaking players don't wake it); a leash keeps it closed.

Without a shop it wanders up to 16 blocks around; once a key is linked, it stays put. Killed, it forgets its owner and links.
book.steveparty.guide.shops.villager_blo: A **piston facing down** that extends onto an adult villager's head squashes it into a **Villager Block**: alive, keeping its trades and job, with about 70 reactions. A sticky piston pulls the villager back out.

Put the Villager Block **on the block to imitate**, then **fall on it** from high enough: 10 + 4 × that block's hardness (hay 12, stone 16, planks 18). A **Boxed Trader** pops out, disguised as that block.

The squashed villager's own trades don't carry over.
book.steveparty.guide.stars_mula.dice_fo: Power Star, obsidian, a blast furnace and a netherite ingot.
book.steveparty.guide.stars_mula.ephemer:
A night of shooting stars, rolled once per night at dusk: 25% on a full moon, less as the moon wanes, none on a new moon. Guaranteed on a full moon near a max-level Dice Forge.

6 waves of stars cross the sky above each player. After the first one, a group of **3-5 Mulas** lands **150-600 blocks** away, in the direction the stars went.
book.steveparty.guide.stars_mula.forging:
Click the arrow between the blank faces and the die (**FORGE**): one die every 5 s, in a loop, while ingredients last. Each die uses its blank faces and one fragment per non-black slot.

Hoppers fill it (top and sides) and take dice out from below. Powered = production on. A comparator reads the output.

A **Forged Die** rolls one of its own faces, weighted: a face carved 10 times comes up 10 times as often. A single face makes a loaded die.

Forged dice with the same faces stack and can make a Double or Triple Dice.
book.steveparty.guide.stars_mula.fragmen: 9 fragments make a glowing, glass-like block that breaks back into 9.
book.steveparty.guide.stars_mula.gravity:
Placed, it glows and **pulls** everything within 8 blocks into an orbit, without fall damage; full iron armour (or heavier) resists. Mulas and pawns are never pulled.

Its real job: waking up the **Dice Forge**.
Crying obsidian, 4 black star fragments and a heavy core.
book.steveparty.guide.stars_mula.mula.pa:
A small flying star creature. Mulas come in **blue, red, green, yellow, purple** and, rarely, **black**. They fall from the sky on an **Ephemeride** night, or hatch from a spawn egg.

A Mula only eats food of **its own colour**: the item tooltip says *Mula food: <colour>*. Right-click it with the food.

Satiety goes up to **40** and the Mula grows up to ×3. Full, it **bursts**: it drops **64 star fragments** of its colour (a black one: 1) and flies off as a shooting star, to be reborn 100-400 blocks away, same Mula, empty belly.

The best source of star fragments!
book.steveparty.guide.stars_mula.mula_ho:
A forge with its core becomes the **home** of every Mula within 16 blocks. They stay around it and **dance** together around the core: ten figures of 26 s each, from the Carousel of Stars to the Heartbeat Nova.

A Mula bursting at home loops back and lands 2-4 blocks from the forge. Explode the core and they all scatter, without fragments.
book.steveparty.guide.stars_mula.name: Stars & the Mula
book.steveparty.guide.stars_mula.power_s:
A rare, always shining item: one fragment each of **blue, green, yellow, red and purple**, or **5 black** fragments.

It crowns the Dice Forge recipe and is the default **Star** of a party.
book.steveparty.guide.stars_mula.rising_:
The core rises with the fragments inside: 16 blocks × fragments / 320 (a black one counts as 64). With all 5 slots full, it is at the top: the forge is at **max level** and guarantees an Ephemeride on full moon nights.

The raised core pulls things into orbit (up to 32 blocks). Hit it and it **explodes**: no block broken, but the core is lost. Sneak with an empty hand to take it back safely.
Right-click a wild Mula with a fragment of **its own colour**: 1 chance in 3. Tamed, it follows you like a balloon, orbits your head when you stand still, and sits when you right-click it empty-handed.

At night, Mulas on a **leash** can lift you into the sky: one big Mula, two half-full ones, or three of any size.
book.steveparty.guide.stars_mula.telesco: Replays past Ephemeride nights. At night, under a clear sky, right-click it: scroll to pick a night, then keep a shooting star in the crosshair until the gauge fills. A **guide star** then lights up above the spot where the Mulas landed.
book.steveparty.guide.tooltip: Build a board, run a party, tame a Mula.
